title: Altitude component contract
description: Per-component, per-project contract: the canvas-expressible API surface (props, events, slots, states, anatomy, token bindings, a11y facts, Figma/code bindings) emitted from the repo's own generated artifacts (CEM, token-map, measure-components output, parity manifest). Adapted from southleft/ds-contracts-poc's contracts/contract.schema.json — see .altitude/contracts/README.md § Deviations for every field dropped or reshaped. Contracts REFERENCE design tokens by their `--al-*` custom-property name; they never define token values.

$schema.description: Relative path back to this schema, e.g. "../contract.schema.json".

id.description: The custom-element tag name, e.g. "al-button". Doubles as the contract's stable identifier.

name.description: Human-readable display name — the Figma component-set name when mapped, else a title-cased derivation of the tag.

version.description: Contract schema-instance version, independent of the component's own package version. Freshly seeded (--seed) contracts start at 0.1.0; adoption into editable source (status: "source") bumps this to 1.0.0. Bump it again on any hand-authored breaking edit to the contract (T10).

status.description: "derived" — machine-generated, not yet hand-reviewed (scripts/contracts/emit-contracts.mjs's --seed output, before adoption). "source" — ADOPTED: this contract is editable, git-tracked source of truth (T10, spec 2026-08-25-contract-backed-figma-parity-and-generation); the emitter no longer regenerates it, hand edits are the reviewable unit of change (contract PR), and drift is checked against it with --check-drift rather than the other way around. "draft" / "stable" / "deprecated" are reserved for a further maturity phase on top of "source".

description.description: The CEM's class-level description. Currently boilerplate ("Component: al-button") for every Altitude component — see README § Deviations.

element.description: The rendered host HTML element (e.g. "button"), read from measured anatomy. `null` when anatomy is unavailable.

role.description: ARIA role, when the CEM or measured anatomy names one. `null` when not determinable from canvas-expressible facts (no live accessibility-tree read is performed).

name.description: The HTML attribute name, as CEM records it (component authors use camelCase attribute names directly, e.g. "isDisabled").

type.description: Normalized from the CEM's TypeScript type text. A type that is a clean union of quoted string literals becomes "enum" with `values` populated; everything else falls back to "boolean" / "number" / "string" by best-effort text match, or "string" as the default.

rawType.description: The CEM's original TypeScript type text, preserved verbatim (e.g. "boolean | 'mixed'") for cases the normalized `type` cannot represent losslessly.

values.description: Present only when type is "enum" — the legal literal values, sorted.

default.description: The prop's default value, when the CEM records one.

member.description: The backing class field name, when it differs from the attribute name.

kind.description: The Figma component-property type, as observed by scripts/figma-parity/refresh-figma-digests.mjs.

property.description: The Figma component-property name (Title Case, e.g. "Variant").

options.description: The raw Figma option labels for a VARIANT property, as observed — NOT mapped value-for-value onto `values` (see README § Deviations: label pairing across the two sides is not attempted here).

axis.description: OPTIONAL, hand-curated (T23, spec 2026-08-25-contract-backed-figma-parity-and-generation). PROPERTY MODE IS THE LIBRARY DEFAULT AS OF T31: the real convention across this library's hand-built sets is a LEAN set (State x Variant variants only) with slot/layout booleans expressed as shared BOOLEAN component properties, never as fanned-out VARIANT axes — al-button's own contract no longer curates anything into axis mode (see .altitude/contracts/README.md § Fan-out convention). This field, and the axis-mode fan-out machinery that reads it, remain fully supported for a future component whose REAL Figma set demonstrably fans a boolean out as its own axis — curate `true` there, deliberately, per that set's confirmed live shape, not as a default. When true, this prop should FAN OUT as a Figma VARIANT axis (its own True/False option column, cartesian with every other axis) in a generated set, rather than staying a single shared component PROPERTY. Only meaningful alongside `kind: "VARIANT"` (a boolean prop marked as an axis reads `options: ["False", "True"]`, Figma's own Title Case boolean-variant spelling). Every non-curated boolean is ALSO fanned out this same way, unconditionally, by `generate-figma.mjs --sheet` (T31) — a separate, plugin-free documentation mode that builds a labeled grid of INSTANCES of the (property-mode) generated set next to it, one per property combination, rather than baking the fan-out into the set's own variants.

omit.description: OPTIONAL, hand-curated OPT-OUT (T27, spec 2026-08-25-contract-backed-figma-parity-and-generation): true when this prop should NOT be expressed in a generated Figma set at all — no axis, no component property, no instance — reserving the right to keep a code-only prop out of the design surface entirely (e.g. al-button's `fullWidth`, owner's call: "I don't need that in figma"). Mutually exclusive with `axis` in practice (an omitted prop has nothing left to fan out); when `omit` is true this object typically carries no other keys — there is nothing else to record about a Figma binding this prop deliberately has none of. The differ treats an omitted prop as a named `skipped` fact (`reason: "intentional-omission"`), never a `missing-in-canvas` disagreement — but a canvas property THAT STILL PAIRS to an omitted prop's name IS flagged (kind `present-despite-omission`), since the curation says it should not be there. See .altitude/contracts/README.md § Figma-expression opt-out.

pairWith.description: OPTIONAL, hand-curated PAIRING (2026-08-27): names the Figma component-property this code prop pairs with, for the case where the two sides deliberately use DIFFERENT names for the same axis and no normalisation can bridge them — al-divider's code prop `variant` is the Figma set's `Orientation` axis, because "orientation" is what a designer reads on the canvas and "variant" is what the CEM calls it. `normKey` only lowercases, strips non-alphanumerics, and strips the is/has prefixes in NAME_ALIAS_PREFIXES, so a genuinely semantic rename is UNDERIVABLE and has to be curated. Only the PAIRING is hand-owned: `kind` and `options` are still derived from the parity manifest's observed digest of the real set (refresh-figma-digests.mjs), so this can never assert a Figma axis that is not actually there — if the named property disappears from Figma the whole binding drops back to `null` and --check-drift reports it, exactly like an unaliased prop.

figma.description: `null` when this prop has no matched, OBSERVED Figma component property (never-refreshed manifest, or a prop the Figma set does not expose).

name.description: Empty string for the default (unnamed) slot.

figmaPlaceholder.description: OPTIONAL, hand-authored (T19, spec 2026-08-25-contract-backed-figma-parity-and-generation): the name of the icon component this slot's Icon Before/After INSTANCE_SWAP property defaults to. As of T28, this name is resolved against the PHOSPHOR Figma library (e.g. "check-circle", "paper-plane") — NEVER the legacy local "🛠 Icons" page, which scripts/contracts/generate-figma.mjs no longer looks up at all. A name, never a node id/key — library components re-mint ids on republish; generate-figma.mjs resolves the actual component BY NAME at generation time (findPhosphorComponentByName), which may itself fail to find a match in a given environment (no team-library component enumeration exists in the Figma plugin API; see .altitude/contracts/README.md § Phosphor icon source for the resolution mechanism and its honest limits) — a resolution failure degrades to no icon instance/property, never a silent fallback to the old page. Absent when no placeholder has been discovered/decided for this slot yet; generate-figma.mjs then builds the Slot Before/After boolean only (or the axis, if curated), with no Icon Before/After property or instance.

figmaAxis.description: OPTIONAL, hand-curated (T23, spec 2026-08-25-contract-backed-figma-parity-and-generation). PROPERTY MODE IS THE LIBRARY DEFAULT AS OF T31 — al-button's own contract no longer curates either slot this way (its real Figma set keeps Slot Before/Slot After as plain BOOLEAN properties; see .altitude/contracts/README.md § Fan-out convention for the corrected reading of the Propstar reference this curation was originally based on). When true, this `before`/`after` slot should FAN OUT as its own True/False Figma VARIANT axis ("Slot Before"/"Slot After") in a generated set — cartesian with every other axis, each combination a separately-built variant with the slot's icon statically shown or hidden — rather than a single shared BOOLEAN component property toggling visibility across every variant at once. Absent/false is the default (boolean property, T12/T18/T19/T31 behavior) — curate `true` only for a component whose real (or intended) Figma set demonstrably fans it out. Every non-curated slot boolean is ALSO fanned out this same way, unconditionally, by `generate-figma.mjs --sheet` (T31)'s plugin-free documentation-sheet mode — a labeled grid of INSTANCES of the (property-mode) generated set, one per property combination, built next to the set rather than baked into its own variants.

figmaOmit.description: OPTIONAL, hand-curated OPT-OUT (T27, spec 2026-08-25-contract-backed-figma-parity-and-generation): true when this slot should NOT be expressed in a generated Figma set at all — no axis, no BOOLEAN property, no icon instance, no Icon Before/After INSTANCE_SWAP property. Mutually exclusive with `figmaAxis` in practice. The differ treats an omitted slot as a named `skipped` fact (`reason: "intentional-omission"`), never a `slot-unpaired` disagreement — but a canvas property that still pairs to an omitted slot's name/convention IS flagged (kind `present-despite-omission`). See .altitude/contracts/README.md § Figma-expression opt-out.

tag.description: An al-* component this component's OWN source renders internally. A trailing "-*" (e.g. "al-icon-*") records a dynamically-interpolated tag family (`<al-icon-${...}>`) — a real nesting fact whose concrete member is chosen at runtime.

evidence.description: How the nesting was observed in source: "template" — a literal `<al-...` tag in the component's render; "import" — a sibling component module import (composites import the classes of the components they instantiate under the registry's scoped-tag model, so an import is nesting evidence even when the tag is built dynamically).

composition.description: DERIVED (spec 2026-08-26-contract-coverage…): the code-side NESTING graph — which other al-* components this component renders inside itself, from a deterministic scan of its own committed source (never fabricated, never hand-curated; --refresh re-derives it). This is the contract fact a generator MUST honor for molecules/organisms: a composed component's Figma set nests INSTANCES of these components' own sets rather than rebuilding their internals as raw frames. `null` only when the component's source file could not be read in this environment.

states.description: Interaction states actually captured by scripts/figma-atoms/measure-components.mjs for this component. Empty when anatomy is unavailable — see `anatomySource`.

anatomySource.description: "measured" — `anatomy` was built from a real measure-components.mjs run. "unavailable" — no measured output existed on disk for this tag; `anatomy` is null. Never fabricated.

anatomyCase.description: The variant `case` string (e.g. "Variant=default,Width=hug") sampled to build `anatomy`, for traceability. `null` when anatomySource is "unavailable".

cases.description: DERIVED (spec 2026-08-26-contract-coverage…, Breadcrumbs Item walkthrough): the FULL anatomy tree of EVERY measured default-state case, sorted by case string. `root`/`anatomyCase` remain the sampled base (back-compat); these are what let a generator fan a measured case DIMENSION (Current, Separator, Shape…) out as a real Figma variant axis with each combination built from its own true structure — a separator child that only exists in Separator=yes cases, a dot form that replaces the label. Structural facts, not just token deltas, so this is full trees rather than a diff format.

stateOverrides.description: Per-state token deltas against `root`, keyed by node PATH ("0" = root, "0.1" = its second child, etc. — see anatomyNode traversal order). Only nodes/tokens that actually differ from the default state are present; a state absent here means the same case had no captured delta.

tokens.description: Every `--al-*` custom property referenced anywhere in `anatomy` (root, descendants, and state overrides), deduplicated and sorted. This is a REFERENCE list — token values live in the token pipeline (libs/al-web-components/styles/tokens), never here.

variant.description: Keyed by the SAME lowercase values the `variant` prop's `values`/`bindings.figma.options` already use (BEM modifier class suffix -> variant value, e.g. `.al-c-button--secondary` -> "secondary"), PLUS a synthesized default-variant key for the component's unmodified base selector when exactly one Figma option has no corresponding modifier class (e.g. Button's bare `.al-c-button` rule -> "primary"). Each entry is CSS property -> token binding for that variant's own declarations (T18, spec 2026-08-25-contract-backed-figma-parity-and-generation).

state.description: Keyed by the SAME state names `states` already uses (pseudo-class/attribute -> state: `:hover` -> "hover", `:focus-visible`/`:focus` -> "focus", `:active` -> "active", `:disabled`/`[disabled]` -> "disabled"). CSS property -> token binding for the GENERIC (variant-agnostic) state rule nested under the component's unmodified base selector — applies to any variant that has no compound override under `variant.<name>.state.<name>`.

^(?!variant$|state$)[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$.description: T25: an enum prop OTHER than `variant` whose BEM modifier classes (`.al-c-<tag>--<value>`) carry their own token-bearing declarations — e.g. Badge's `position` (top-left/top-right/bottom-left/bottom-right share one `z-index` rule). Keyed by the prop's own name; each entry keyed by that prop's lowercase values, same conditionBindingMap/variantBinding shape as `variant` above. Kept fully separate from `variant`'s own key/semantics — never merged into it, even when a component has both.

conditionalBindings.description: Per-variant and per-state CSS declaration -> token bindings recovered directly from the component's own .scss (T18) — never fabricated: a component whose .scss has no BEM modifier classes or no nested pseudo-class/attribute state rules simply omits the corresponding key (or the whole section). Only declarations whose value resolves to EXACTLY ONE `--al-*` design token (or the `border: <width> solid <color>` two-token shorthand, split into `border-width`/`border-color`; or a two-level `var(--al-A, var(--al-B))` role/fallback chain, resolved to whichever of the two this project's own token tree actually indexes — T25) are captured — a value with an unresolvable custom property (e.g. `--al-button-padding`) or more than one uncorrelated token reference is skipped rather than guessed. This is DERIVED from source that IS available in CI (unlike measured anatomy), so it participates fully in --check-drift and --check-determinism.

ariaAttributes.description: CEM attribute names that carry ARIA semantics (name matches /aria/i), e.g. "ariaControls".

cssParts.description: Named `::part()` targets the CEM records — the styleable/inspectable surface for an AT or a design tool.

workspace.description: The npm workspace this component ships from (the shared library, or a project's brandLibrary).

tag.description: The rendered HTML tag for this node.

cls.description: The node's authored class, when present.

text.description: DERIVED (spec 2026-08-26-contract-coverage…, Checkbox walkthrough): the node's rendered text content as measured (capped at 300 chars) — the breadcrumbs '/' separator, a checkbox's 'Checkbox label', a button's 'Button'. Present only on nodes the measurement pass saw text in. This supersedes the interim figma.gen.json textContent curation for components measured after the field landed.

box.description: DERIVED (spec 2026-08-26-contract-coverage…, Checkbox walkthrough): the node's measured rendered size, rounded to 0.1px. A deliberate revision of the T12-era 'no pixel geometry' rule: container ARRANGEMENT stays coarse (flex facts + tokens — this is still not a layout DSL), but a leaf GLYPH's fixed size (an 18×18 custom-check square, a 40×40 hit target) is itself a canvas-expressible code fact — Sass size() literals never surface as custom-property tokens, so without this a generated checkbox has no box at all. Generators use it for childless glyph nodes; a 0×0 box marks a node invisible in this case (a resting ripple) and is skipped.

component.description: DERIVED (spec 2026-08-26-contract-coverage…): present when this node IS another component's root — its class list carries that component's own `al-c-<name>` BEM block class (measured anatomy flattens shadow boundaries, so a nested al-checkbox appears as `div.al-c-checkbox`). The node's subtree is that component's INTERNALS: a generator should place an INSTANCE of that component's set here (same by-name discipline as the DS Icon wrapper) instead of rebuilding the subtree as raw frames. Never set on the anatomy root itself (path "0" is this contract's own component).

wrap.description: `flex-wrap`, recorded ONLY when the node genuinely wraps — measure-lib.js nulls the `nowrap` initial value rather than storing it on every node (measure-lib.js:431). Reaches Figma as `layoutWrap` via build-set-code.mjs's layoutWrapsFor, which Figma honours on HORIZONTAL auto-layout only; `display: grid` implies WRAP regardless of this value.

grow.description: `flex-grow`, recorded ONLY when non-zero — measure-lib.js nulls the 0 initial value rather than storing it on every node. This is the only captured fact that means FILL rather than hug: build-set-code.mjs turns it into `layoutSizingHorizontal`/`layoutSizingVertical` = 'FILL' along the PARENT's main axis. Without it every generated frame hugs, which is why a filling message rendered at its max-content width and overflowed its own container.

alignSelf.description: `align-self`, recorded ONLY when the child overrides its parent's cross-axis alignment — measure-lib.js nulls the 'auto'/'normal' initial values (same discipline as wrap/grow). Consumers combine it with the parent's `align` when deciding cross-axis FILL: a child that opts out of stretch (e.g. `align-self: flex-start`) must not fill even under a stretching parent (spec 2026-08-28-layout-fill-and-grow-facts).

layout.description: Coarse, canvas-expressible layout facts (no pixel geometry) computed from the measured node.

tokens.description: CSS property name -> token binding REFERENCED by this node in its default state.

code.description: The `--al-*` custom property this CSS declaration resolves to.

figma.description: The matching Figma variable path from scripts/figma-atoms/token-map.mjs (e.g. "theme/color/background/primary-default"), or null when token-map has no entry for this token.

nodeTokenDiff.description: Node path -> { cssProperty -> token binding } for tokens that changed (or newly appeared) in this state, relative to the same path in `root`.

conditionBindingMap.description: CSS property -> token binding recovered from ONE selector's direct declarations (T18).

state.description: Compound variant+state overrides found as a pseudo-class/attribute rule NESTED directly inside this variant's own selector block (e.g. `.al-c-button--secondary:hover`) — wins over the generic `conditionalBindings.state.<name>` for this variant.

parts.description: T25: sub-element overrides found as a REVERSED-nesting BEM rule — `.al-c-<tag>__<part> { .al-c-<tag>--<this-variant> & {...} }` (this repo's authored convention for "this part looks different inside that variant", verified in alert/banner/toast's `__icon` rules; e.g. the icon's `--al-icon-fill` recolors per tone). Keyed by the part's own BEM suffix (`icon`, not `__icon`).

variantBinding.description: One variant's own CSS property -> token bindings (additionalProperties), plus an optional `state` map for its compound state overrides and an optional `parts` map for sub-element overrides. `state` and `parts` are reserved and never collide with a real CSS property name.
